datasets.description: Every company (account) with its firmographics, tier and enrichment.
Every person in the workspace with their profile, status, owner and relationship scores.
Deals: the live pipeline rail. Status is derived from outcome (null = open). Opportunities: the retiring rail, kept read-only. Same thing as a deal; the rail column tells them apart.
Pipelines the deals move through.
Stages per pipeline. stage_type (active, won, lost) is the canonical stage mapping.
Which people are attached to which deals.
Stakeholder maps per deal: role, influence, support and concerns.
Buying committee members per deal.
Activities logged against deals.
Every stage move with how long the deal sat in the previous stage.
Comments on deals.
Service lines priced on each deal.
Every recorded touch with a person: emails, meetings, calls, messages and manual notes of contact.
The older activity log per person.
Imported email messages linked to a person (text bodies, no HTML). Messages not linked to a person are not reachable by workspace and are left out.
Thread-level summaries, commitments and signals.
Emails sent from Nynch (text bodies).
LinkedIn messages imported from the extension.
WhatsApp, Slack and other chat messages synced to a person.
Meeting records with summaries, commitments and full transcripts (also written to transcripts/).
Imported calendar events and their attendees.
Who attended which meeting.
Notes written on people.
Teammate comments on people, companies and deals.
Team tasks.
Personal action items tied to people and deals.
Promises made and received.
Commitments confirmed as genuine from conversations.
Which people belong to which companies, including secondary associations.
Past and present roles per person.
Every email address per person with consent and deliverability state.
What a person is to the firm on an account, agreement, project or deal.
Company signals as the workspace sees them (funding, hiring, leadership, news).
Detected changes about a person (job moves, title changes).
Social activity signals per person.
Buying signals spotted in conversations.
Revenue signals (expansion, upsell, referral angles). These are signals, not deals.
Intelligence items surfaced about people and companies.
Two-way engagement scores per person; the inputs to the warmth tier.
Ideal client profiles.
The services the firm sells.
Proof points and evidence the firm uses.
The customer problems the firm solves.
Competitors and how the firm wins against them.
Positioning manifestos.
Custom field definitions.
Custom field values per record.
The workspace lead-source list.
The synthesised relationship memory per person: history, facts, what not to assume.
The synthesised account memory per company.
Durable memories Nynch agents kept about people, workflows and preferences.
Knowledge-graph entities for people, companies and deals.
Known facts: relationships between people, companies and deals with their evidence.
Buyer beliefs the firm has catalogued.
Each time a belief was observed in a conversation.
Patterns learned from won and lost deals.
Patterns learned from proposals.
Decisions recorded with their reasoning.
Warm introduction requests and their outcomes.
Introduction asks between teammates.
Warm paths to target people through connectors.
Circles of leverage around a target.
Members of each circle.
Proposals with their full content (also written to proposals/).
Every proposal version as a frozen document.
Priced options inside proposals.
Where each proposal was exported to (links to the generated documents).
Commercial agreements per account.
Accepted versions of each agreement with frozen terms.
Service lines inside accepted agreement versions.
Delivery projects per account.
Outreach campaigns and their steps.
Who was enrolled in which campaign and what happened.
Company briefs written for prospects.

counts_note: counts_from_sql is count(*) at the moment each dataset started; the workspace stays live during an export, so a row added or deleted while a dataset was being read can make the two differ by that much.
